data.name: Vanna
data.gender_notes: Vanna is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Vanna was the goddess of fertility, birth, and the weaving loom. She was also known as the protector of women in childbirth. In Christianity, Vanna can be seen as a symbol of the Virgin Mary, who brought new life into the world through her son, Jesus. The name Vanna carries the meaning “Goddess of fertility” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Vanna usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of fertility and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of the divine feminine and the power of creation.
data.etymology: Vanna belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of fertility.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vanna total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vanna, with its roots in Greek mythology, carries a rich cultural heritage as the goddess of fertility, birth, and weaving. It represents the powerful and essential role of women in the creation of new life and the weaving of the fabric of society.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Vanna can be seen as a symbol of the Virgin Mary, who brought new life into the world through her son, Jesus, and continued to nurture and protect humanity as a devoted and loving mother. Vanna represents the divine feminine, and the strength and grace embodied in the Blessed Mother, whom Christians look to for intercession, guidance, and inspiration.
